perOption.reason: Seam: 'meet within + a timeframe' is a natural temporal collocation; participle 'freed from break-induced remoteness' post-modifies grammatically. Logic: exactly restates the passage's remedy — reframe the period ('this winter' instead of 'next year') so that the break no longer induces the sense of remoteness that delays action. Entailed by both the problem statement (break -> remote -> inaction) and the prescribed fix.

Grammatical, but logically over-quantified. The passage does not abolish calendar boundaries; it substitutes one calendar unit ('this winter' — itself a bounded unit) for another so the deadline falls inside the same unit. The universal 'every calendar boundary has been removed' is falsified by the text's own example.

Category error at the seam: 'meet a challenge within a workload' — 'within' requires a temporal container here, and 'workload' is an amount of work, not a timeframe. Logic also reversed: manageable stress is stated as a consequence of the reframing ('That way the stress is more manageable'), not a pre-existing condition ('has already been fully reduced').

Contradicts the example: the deadline is in January, so the reframed interval (November to January, 'this winter') necessarily DOES stretch past the New Year; the whole point is that it crosses the break while being conceived as one continuous unit. Additionally 'alone' is a dangling adverb with no determinate scope (New Year? stretch?), weakening grammaticality.

Grammatical but logically inverted: the passage treats a break as a demotivating boundary whose effect must be neutralized, never as something to 'deliberately use as a motivator.' No sentence supports breaks having motivational value.

note: Lens: grammarian/logician. Only option 1 satisfies both the syntactic seam (within + temporal NP) and the passage's entailment (eliminate break-induced remoteness by reframing the unit). Options 2 and 5 are grammatical distractors defeated purely on logic (over-quantification and polarity inversion respectively); 3 fails on both collocation and causal order; 4 is contradicted by the passage's own Nov-to-Jan example and carries a scope-ambiguous 'alone'. No alternative parse (reduced relative, participial, etc.) rescues any distractor. Single defensible answer.
